title: Huxley-Gödel Machine: Human-Level Coding Agent Development by an Approximation of the Optimal Self-Improving Machine
mutable_substrate: A self-referential coding-agent repository/scaffold represented as nodes in an ancestry tree; an agent uses LLM queries plus file-editing and bash tools (or bash alone in the full SWE-bench Verified experiment) to create modified child agents.
optimization_operator: LLM-driven repository self-modification creates a child from a selected parent. HGM changes the outer-loop search: clade-level Beta/Thompson sampling selects parents, agent-level Thompson sampling selects evaluations, and a UCB-Air-inspired widening rule chooses expansion versus evaluation.
feedback_selection: Binary pass/fail outcomes on SWE-bench or Polyglot tasks update per-agent and ancestral clade success/failure counts. Expansion is guided by estimated Clade-Metaproductivity rather than current node accuracy; final selection uses a posterior best-belief criterion.
archive_memory: A rooted tree preserves every agent and its parent-child lineage. Each descendant evaluation updates aggregate counts for all ancestors, so ancestry is an active shared-memory structure used to estimate lineage productivity.
validation_strategy: Controlled equal-ancestor and 800-evaluation comparisons with DGM and SICA; post-hoc leakage-controlled correlation against empirical clade maxima; full 500-task SWE-bench Verified optimization; transfer to 207 nonoverlapping SWE-bench Lite tasks and the standard 300-task set; matched-backbone local SWE-agent comparison; and model transfer from GPT-5-mini to GPT-5. No repeated-run uncertainty or component ablations are reported.
adaptation_mode: Offline asynchronous tree search over self-modified agent versions under a fixed compute/evaluation budget. Expansion and one-task evaluation jobs run concurrently; a best-belief agent is selected at the end rather than adapting the released agent continually at runtime.
benchmarks: SWE-bench Lite filtered (207 tasks after excluding 93 overlaps)
principal_results: HGM estimated CMP has weighted Pearson correlation 0.778 on SWE-Verified-60 and 0.626 on Polyglot versus 0.285/0.383 for DGM and 0.444/0.274 for SICA.

Under 800 evaluations, HGM reaches 56.7% on SWE-Verified-60 using 517 allocated CPU-hours, versus DGM's 53.3% and 1,231 hours; SICA reaches 50.0% but stops after 360 evaluations due to repeated context-window errors.
Under 800 Polyglot evaluations, HGM reaches 30.5% using 347 allocated CPU-hours, versus DGM's 27.1%/2,385 hours and SICA's 25.4%/572 hours.
On full SWE-bench Verified, 8,000 evaluations improve the initial GPT-5-mini agent from 53.2% to 61.4%.
On SWE-bench Lite with GPT-5-mini, the evolved scaffold scores 40.1% filtered and 49.0% standard versus its ancestor's 34.8%/44.0% and a locally adapted SWE-agent's 39.6%/47.6%.

After swapping the evolved scaffold to GPT-5, it scores 47.8% filtered and 57.0% standard versus the contemporary officially checked SWE-agent reference's 48.3%/56.7%, establishing within-one-task parity in the paper's human-design comparison.
Under a restrictive static, repeatable, terminal-utility setting, the paper proves that access to exact policy-dependent CMP is sufficient to reproduce Gödel-Machine accept/reject behavior.
limitations: The theorem assumes an exact CMP oracle, free proofs, unit-cost modifications, known utility, repeatable trials, a static environment, and only terminal utility; it does not prove practical HGM optimal.
The empirical estimator is an evaluation-weighted clade mean, while formal CMP is an expected future maximum; no approximation-error bound is given.
Empirical CMP is endogenous to the method-generated tree and can favor clades receiving more expansion and evaluation opportunities.
No independent search replications, confidence intervals, or ablations isolate CMP from asynchronous scheduling, single-task evaluation, widening, or final selection.
SICA fails after 360 SWE-Verified-60 evaluations, preventing a completed equal-budget comparison in that setting.
The human-level claim is benchmark-, model-, date-, and scaffold-design-specific, with one-task differences in both standard and filtered SWE-bench Lite.
Table 1 reports 0.873 for HGM's unweighted Polyglot correlation while prose reports 0.8783; the final beta-posterior selection notation is also ambiguous.
Generated agents receive bash access, but no security threat model, sandbox, harmful-modification audit, or rollback protocol is reported.
safety_controls: Agent execution is time-limited to one hour in controlled experiments and five hours in the full-benchmark experiment.
Polyglot agents cannot access private tests or test outcomes.
The filtered SWE-bench Lite evaluation removes all 93 tasks overlapping with the optimization benchmark.
API support, timeout handling, and LLM interaction-length limits are added to the DGM-derived ancestor.
No broader sandboxing, permission boundary, secret isolation, or adversarial safety control is documented.

explicit_predecessors.name: Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM)
explicit_predecessors.evidence: HGM adopts DGM's self-modifying repository tree, official initial agent, progressive SWE-Verified-60 setup, and baseline protocol, then replaces immediate-performance parent guidance with clade statistics and decouples expansion from evaluation.

explicit_predecessors.name: Self-Improving Coding Agent (SICA)
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Direct search-policy baseline and conceptual predecessor
explicit_predecessors.evidence: SICA also edits its own repository and execution-validates descendants; HGM explicitly targets SICA's greedy current-performance selection and full evaluation of each newest child.

explicit_predecessors.name: Gödel Machine
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The paper defines exact clade metaproductivity as a policy action value and proves that, under restrictive assumptions, its oracle can implement the Gödel Machine's accept/reject policy; HGM is motivated as an empirical approximation.

explicit_predecessors.name: Gödel Agent
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The related-work section identifies Gödel Agent and STOP as early experiments in agents modifying their own scaffolding before repository-level DGM and SICA.

explicit_predecessors.name: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP)
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The related-work section explicitly places STOP with Gödel Agent as a precursor to full software-project self-modification.

explicit_predecessors.name: UCB-Air and infinite-armed bandits
explicit_predecessors.evidence: HGM treats evaluations as pulls of known arms and expansions as creation of new arms, using the UCB-Air condition N_t^alpha >= |T_t| to widen the agent tree.

open_questions: Can latent metaproductivity be evaluated off-policy or with matched subtree budgets to remove search-attention bias?
Does clade guidance outperform node accuracy when asynchronous execution, evaluation granularity, widening, prompts, and final selection are held fixed?
Which estimator best approximates the expected future maximum in the formal CMP definition?
How stable are final accuracy, CPU-hours, correlations, and lineage structure across independent stochastic search runs?
How should unequal task, model-call, expansion, and failure costs enter a cost-aware allocation policy?
Does the discovered scaffold transfer beyond the SWE-bench family, including different languages, long-horizon development, and security tasks?
What provenance, semantic-diff, invariant-checking, sandboxing, and rollback mechanisms can keep deep self-modification trees auditable?

Can the Gödel-Machine connection be extended to costly reasoning, nonrepeatable and changing environments, intermediate rewards and harms, imperfect utility knowledge, and heterogeneous modification costs?
